answers.a: It reaches a final state with non-empty stack

questions.question: In a PDA transition δ(q, a, X) = (p, α), what does each component represent?

answers.a: q is next state, a is stack symbol, X is input, p is current state, α is new input
answers.b: q is current state, a is input symbol, X is top of stack, p is next state, α is stack replacement
answers.c: q is initial state, a is final symbol, X is empty stack, p is accepting state, α is input string
answers.d: q is stack top, a is next state, X is current state, p is input symbol, α is output

questions.question: What is the difference between a DFA and a PDA?

answers.a: A PDA uses a stack, while a DFA does not
answers.b: A DFA recognizes context-free languages, while a PDA recognizes regular languages
answers.c: A PDA can only recognize finite languages
answers.d: A DFA can use a stack, while a PDA cannot

questions.question: What is an epsilon (ε) transition in a PDA?

answers.a: A transition that erases the entire stack
answers.b: A transition that occurs without reading any input symbol
answers.c: A transition that only works when the stack is empty
answers.d: A transition that rejects the input string
